gaps.sentence: He gave me ___ useful advice about the paperwork.
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable — never 'an advice'. Use 'a piece of advice' for one item.

gaps.sentence: ___ poverty remains a serious problem in many large cities.
gaps.explanation: Uncountable abstract nouns in a general sense take no article.

gaps.sentence: She goes to the gym twice ___ week.
gaps.explanation: 'Twice a week' — rates take 'a' (= per). The other gap is 'the gym'.

gaps.sentence: He had ___ operation on his knee last year.
gaps.explanation: 'Operation' starts with a vowel sound, so 'an operation'.

gaps.sentence: ___ water in this bottle tastes strange.
gaps.explanation: The of/in-phrase makes the noun definite: the water in this bottle.

gaps.sentence: He found ___ coin buried in the sand.
gaps.explanation: 'A coin' first mention; 'in the sand' — sand as a mass takes 'the' here (the sand on that beach).

gaps.sentence: She has ___ excellent command of Japanese.
gaps.explanation: 'Have an excellent command of' — 'excellent' starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: ___ number of applicants has doubled this year.
gaps.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb ('has'); 'a number of' would take 'have'.
